title: Booking settings — calendar, rooms, notification addresses
body:
You can reach the booking module's settings screen on the Modules tab, via the **„Beállítás”** link next to the module. Here you manage your calendar, the rooms you rent out, and your notification addresses.

![Screenshot: the "Mikor nem kiadó?" calendar on a phone — with days you have blocked, days booked by a guest, and days booked by another room](assets/hu/screen.png)

## What is where on the screen?

Below the dark header block there is a row of small buttons: **„Mikor nem kiadó?”**, **„Hirdeti máshol is?”**, **„Mit ad ki?”**, **„Foglalás beállítása”**, **„Haladó beállítások”**. This row stays at the top of the screen even while you scroll; tapping a button makes the page jump to that section, and the button for the section you are currently on is always highlighted. On a computer the same list appears on the right-hand edge, titled **„Ezen a lapon”**. The sections of the page are arranged into groups, with a line running from the group title to the edge of the page: the calendar, then **„Portálok”** (connecting Booking.com, Szállás.hu and Airbnb), then **„Szobák és beállítások”** (your rented rooms, the question-by-question setup, and the advanced settings).

## The settings: question by question

Below the calendar and the requests is the **„Foglalás beállítása”** card. The **„Beállítom kérdésről kérdésre”** button opens a separate page where you provide the rooms, prices, periods and booking rules one after another, by answering questions — with a Helper that explains anything you do not understand. This page is described by the "Foglalás beállítása" help article.

The earlier settings form (the fields below: notification address, tourist tax, shortest and longest booking) has been kept: it opens when you tap the **„Haladó beállítások”** row under the card. It records the same data as the question-based page.

## Where do I answer booking requests?

Incoming requests wait on the **„Foglalások”** tab — there you confirm or decline them, with a message to the guest. If a request on this screen is awaiting a decision, a bar signals it, and the **„Foglalások megnyitása”** button takes you there. You can also handle the decision directly from the e-mail you receive about the request, without logging in: the link in the **„Gyors döntés innen is:”** line of the message opens a confirmation page, and there you decide with the **„Igen, elfogadom”** or the **„Igen, elutasítom”** button — the guest only receives a reply after you have decided.

## Where should the notifications arrive?

In the **„Hová küldjük a foglalási kéréseket?”** field (it opens at the bottom of the screen when you tap the **„Haladó beállítások”** row; the **„Foglalás beállítása”** page asks the same thing) you provide the address — you can give several addresses separated by a comma (e.g. reception and owner). The guest's reply also goes to the first address. If you leave it empty, we send it to the e-mail address of your account.

## What does the guest pay on site? (tourist tax)

In the **„Idegenforgalmi adó”** field (it opens at the bottom of the screen when you tap the **„Haladó beállítások”** row; the **„Foglalás beállítása”** page asks the same thing) enter the amount the guest pays **on site**, on top of the accommodation fee — broken down as **HUF / person / night**. On your website this amount is not merged into the price: it stands in a separate box, labelled "Payable on site in addition to this", calculated out (e.g. *500 HUF / person / night × 2 persons × 3 nights = 3,000 HUF*). Guests under 18 are exempt: we do not count those whom the guest marks as children at booking, and the box states this in a sentence.

**If you leave it empty**, an amber-bordered reminder appears under the opened Advanced settings, below the field, and **no amount is shown** on your website — the guest only sees that a tourist tax is payable on site. We do not invent an amount on your behalf: a wrong number does more harm than a missing one. The reminder disappears on its own as soon as you save a value.

The guest also sees the tax **after** sending the request: the same line appears on the confirmation shown on screen ("We have sent your request"), in the "recorded" e-mail and in the confirmation e-mail. The e-mails state the amount that was in effect when the request was sent — if you later change the field, the e-mails of requests already received do not change. On a phone it also appears in the second step of the booking, below the amount, and it updates together with any change in the number of people.

**If you do not charge a tourist tax, enter 0** — and save. This is not the same as leaving it empty: 0 means you have **stated** that there is none, so your website **does not even mention** the tax. An empty field means you have not yet declared it — in that case the page states that a tax is payable on site, without an amount.

⚠️ **The price breakdown only appears if you have a price list.** You provide the prices in the **Árak, szezonok** module (a separate module) — or in the "Prices" section of the "Foglalás beállítása" page. As long as there is not a single price there, the guest can select days in the calendar, but no price — and with it no tourist tax box — appears.

What else is included in the price (e.g. *cleaning, bed linen, towels*) you now provide in the **„Ellátás”** section of the **Árak, szezonok** module, in the **„Mi van még benne az árban?”** field — in the same place as breakfast and half board. Text entered earlier has been kept unchanged.

## Managing the calendar

At the top of the screen there is a dark bar: it contains the name and fee of the module, and below it the **„Vissza a modulokhoz”** link (with a ‹ arrow before it) and the **„Útmutató ehhez a képernyőhöz”** link (which opens this help article).

In the **„Mikor nem kiadó?”** calendar, tap the days on which you cannot receive guests. The **„Naptár mentése”** button saves the change. The ‹ and › arrows let you page between months.

The calendar is **collapsible**: tapping its header row collapses it, and even when collapsed it states how many days are not available that month (for example "3 days not available"; if there are none: **„minden nap kiadó”**). Tapping again opens it.

## The day types — and what each does when tapped

The first three states always appear in the legend, even if there is not a single such day that month. The **„Másik szoba foglalása”** row, however, only appears if there really is such a day — so you often see only the first three:

| Legend | What it means | What happens if you tap it |
|---|---|---|
| **„Szabad”** | A bookable night | It becomes full (dark blue). After saving, the guest cannot book it. |
| **„Ön jelölte: nem kiadó”** | Your own block (medium blue) | **It becomes available again** — this is how you undo it if you can rent it out after all. |
| **„Vendég foglalása”** | An accepted booking (darkest, with a tiny light-blue dot) | **The booking details pop up** — see the next section. It cannot be freed up here. |
| **„Másik szoba foglalása”** | Striped: another room of the property holds it. **Only appears if there is such a day.** | A pop-up shows **which room** and **who** holds it. It cannot be released here. |

## What is behind a booked day?

Tapping a booked day makes **the day's details pop up in the centre of the screen**:

- **For a guest booking**, the guest's name, the period and the number of nights, the number of people, the price (if there was a price list), and their **e-mail address and phone number — both clickable**, so you can call or write to them immediately. If the guest left a message, it can also be read here. Buttons: **„Foglalás megnyitása”** (takes you to the Bookings tab) and **„Írok a vendégnek”**.
- **For a striped day**, which room holds it. If there is a guest booking there, the guest's name and period are shown too, and you can open it with the **„Foglalás megnyitása”** button; but if you simply marked that room not available by hand, the card states: "You marked this day not available in the … calendar". In both cases there is an **„Átváltok a naptárára”** button.

You close the card with the **×** or by tapping the dark background behind it.

## If you also advertise on Booking.com, Szállás.hu or Airbnb

Connect the calendars, so that you do not have to block the same day in two places: what is booked on the portal is also blocked here, and what is booked here is blocked on the portal too. At the top of the **„Hirdeti máshol is?”** (Do you advertise elsewhere too?) card below the calendar, the **„Így köti össze — videó és leírás”** (How to connect it — video and description) section walks you through the whole thing. At the top you choose the portal (Booking.com, Szállás.hu or Airbnb), and below it one of two views: **„Videó”** (Video) shows in 2.5–3 minutes, with Hungarian voice and captions, what to click on the portal and here (it zooms in on every menu item and pauses on it); **„Leírás képekkel”** (Description with images) gives the same steps as numbered pictures, with a frame marking where to click. Tap a picture to see it larger. The video is in Hungarian, so it only appears on the Hungarian interface; in other languages the **„Videó”** button is not shown, and the picture guide opens right away.

Below that, all three portals have their own box, with two steps:

1. **Bring the portal's calendar link here.** On the portal you receive a link in the calendar sync menu (Booking.com: Rates & Availability › Calendar › calendar synchronization; Szállás.hu: Prices and capacity › Calendar sync (iCal); Airbnb: Calendar › Availability › Connect calendars — on the Hungarian interface Árak és elérhetőség › Naptár szinkronizálás, or Naptár › Foglalhatóság › Naptárak bekötése). Paste it into the field and press the **„Összekötés”** button — we check it right away and state how many booked days we brought over.
2. **Give our link to the portal.** The **„Másolás”** button copies it to the clipboard, and you paste it into the same portal menu, where the calendar is imported.

Every box has a **„Segítség: így köti össze lépésről lépésre”** row: opening it guides you through the portal's own menu items. You can break a wrong link with the **„Leválasztás”** button: we ask you on the spot and state how many days brought from the portal will be freed up — only the **„Igen, leválasztom”** button disconnects (the **„Mégsem”** button closes the question). The days brought from the portal then disappear from your calendar.

In the box you also see when it was last updated, and in total how many booked days we brought over from today onward (the badge above the calendar only counts the month you are viewing). Opening the Sync log row shows the last ten updates: when each succeeded and when it failed.

### If the box shows an error or a warning

- **Red "Error" label:** the most recent update failed. The box states when, what happened, and that the booked days brought over earlier remain in effect — a failed update never frees up a day. You also see when it last succeeded. If you received a new link on the portal, disconnect the old one and connect it with the new one. If the error lasts a day, we also send you an e-mail about it — once; if the link works again and later gets stuck again, we notify you again.
- **"The link is not available, or is not a calendar":** the link is not the portal's calendar export, or it cannot be opened. Paste it again from the portal's calendar sync menu.
- **Conflict:** the portal reports as booked a night for which you have already accepted a booking with us. The box states the day and the guest's name, and you also receive an e-mail about it (once per conflict). We do not cancel either booking: you decide which guest you can receive, and settle the other on the portal or at Bookings.
- **"Attention: the portal has now returned an empty calendar":** the portal shows all bookings as available at once, so the days brought over until now have been freed up. This is normal if they were really cancelled there — if not, check the portal's calendar.
- **"We could not interpret … entries precisely":** there is an entry in the portal's calendar that we skipped or treated as one night. Opening it shows you which one. If a booking seen on a portal is missing here, this may be the reason.

The link received with the **„Másolás”** button is different for each portal: from the calendar we give to a portal we leave out the days we received from that very portal — while the other portals do see them.

Good to know:

- Every room must be connected separately — on the portals too the calendar is per room. The whole house does not need its own link: if you rent out room by room, the house's days are the rooms' days.
- Only the booked days are transferred; the price and the guest's details you still manage on the portal.
- It is not instant: we check the portal every hour, and Booking.com checks our calendar every two hours (there you can also refresh immediately with the "Import now" button).
- Booking.com only allows calendar connection if there one room type means one room, and no channel manager is used.

## Rooms, apartments

In the **„Mit ad ki?”** section you add what you rent out: if you have several rooms or apartments, each gets its own calendar, so they can fill up separately. You add a new room by tapping the dashed-bordered **„Új szoba felvétele”** bar, providing the name and the capacity, with the **„Hozzáadás”** button; you can rename an existing one (under the **„Meglévő szobája”** label — with several rooms, **„Meglévő szobái”**), and if you already have several rooms, you can remove it with the **„Törlés”** button — with a single room this button does not appear. If the Prices module is also switched on, the **„Alapár”** can also be provided BEFORE pressing **„Hozzáadás”**, or you can tick the **„Nem adok meg árat — egyedi ajánlatot küldök”** box below it. Neither is mandatory. If there is neither, after saving a yellow line warns you: the **„Árat adok meg”** button takes you to the Pricing page (enter and save the price there), and the **„Nem adok meg árat”** button records on the spot that you send a custom offer. With several rooms there are **tabs** above the calendar: you tap the one whose calendar you want to view. A tab is only given to what the guest can actually book. If you rent out the house only as a whole, the rooms appear in a sentence below the tabs ("bookable together with the house, so it has no separate calendar"), because bookings can only arrive for the house. If you rent out room by room, it is the other way round: the whole house has no tab, and a sentence below the tabs states why ("whoever requests the whole thing selects every room, so it has no separate calendar"). After rewriting the room's name, you save the change with the **„Mentés”** button of the row.

### Several rooms in one request — and the whole house

With several rooms, the guest can book **one or more rooms** in one request, even all of them. In that case the whole house has no separate price and calendar: whoever requests the whole house selects every room and pays the price of the rooms. On the website the guest first selects the days, then ticks the available rooms in the list; the calendar only shows a night as booked if none of the rooms is available for it. You confirm (or decline) the multi-room request as one on the **„Foglalások”** tab — in that case the period becomes booked in the calendar of each selected room, and appears as a plain **„Vendég foglalása”** day for each (not striped).

If you rent out the house **only as a whole**, the situation is reversed: then only the whole house can be booked, and the rooms appear only for presentation. You can tick this on the settings screen of the Rooms, apartments module, on the **„Az egész ház”** card above the grid (**„Csak egyben adom ki”**) — in that case you also provide the house price there.

### Why a day is sometimes striped

The whole house and its rooms exclude each other: if there is a booking for the **whole house** on a day (for example from an earlier request that arrived for the whole house), all of its rooms are **automatically booked** for that day; and if **any of its rooms** is booked, the whole house **cannot be rented out** for that day.

These days appear **striped** in the other room's calendar. There they cannot be freed up (otherwise the same night would be sold twice) — but tapping the day shows you who holds it, and a button lets you switch to that room's calendar. Two rooms do not exclude each other: they fill up independently. Any room can be deleted with the **„Törlés”** button of its row; the whole house only if there is only one room left. The button first asks for confirmation and lists what is lost with the room (blocked days, prices, calendar sync, earlier bookings); the deletion happens with the **„Igen, törlöm”** button. The last room cannot be deleted, nor one for which a request is still awaiting your decision (or one of your offers is awaiting the guest's reply), nor one to which an accepted, not yet concluded booking belongs — in that case, in place of the confirmation, it shows which request holds it, and the **„Foglalások”** button takes you there. The details are in the Rooms, apartments help article.
